transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Greenfield CISO), Tom Reynolds (Engineering Manager), Priya Sharma (Compliance), Marcus Lee (DevOps)

Summary:  (auto) quick posture review of Redwood's SOC 2 / ISO 27001 attestations, trust center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data residency options. Customer heavy focus on controls mapping for a healthcare workload and legal requirements for audit artifacts retention.

Topics: SOC 2 Type II scope, ISO 27001 certificate, Trust Center access, controls mapping template, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs/retention, encryption keys/KMS, data residency (EU), contractual SLAs and breach notification.

Transcript:
[00:00] Daniel (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Daniel Park, account exec for Redwood Inference. Sofia from our security eng team is with me. How are you all doing?
[00:07] Aisha (Greenfield - CISO): Good morning, thanks. Quick note, we're on a tight timeline to complete vendor compliance review for our ML infra pilot. We'll go through SOC 2, ISO, and the specifics around keys and logs.
[00:17] Sofia (Redwood SE): Hi, everyone. I'll lean into the controls and technical questions. We'll try to map our artifacts to your control list.
[00:23] Tom (Greenfield): Sounds good. Marcus is going to chime on DevOps specifics later.
[00:29] Daniel: Great. High level, Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for the hosted platform and we have an ISO 27001 cert. We also provide a Trust Center link where certified reports and our control mappings are available — we'll share access.
[00:42] Priya (Greenfield - Compliance): When you say "control mappings" do you mean a spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks like HIPAA/ISO/SOC?
[00:48] Sofia: Yes, we have a controls mapping that shows which of our controls map to SOC 2 CC and ISO 27001 controls; we also provide a template to help you map to your internal control IDs.
[00:55] Aisha: Perfect. A few concrete asks up front: 1) We need a redactable SOC 2 Type II report; 2) ISO certificate and scope; 3) trust center access for our auditors; 4) clear statements about data residency and KMS.
[01:08] Daniel: All are doable. For trust center we can create auditor access or share bundles. We'll send the redactable report rather than full PII.
[01:16] Marcus (Greenfield - DevOps): On KMS, does Redwood manage keys or can we bring our own (BYOK)? Also question on encryption at rest for dedicated/private deployments.
[01:27] Sofia: Short answer: both. For hosted we offer Redwood-managed encryption with customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) for higher assurance. For Private deployments you can control keys on-prem or via your KMS, yes. We documented key lifecycle and rotation processes in the trust center.
[01:42] Tom: Is there an HSM option?
[01:45] Sofia: We integrate with customer HSM-backed keys through supported KMS providers — if you need FIPS/HSM attestations we can outline the integration approach.
[01:52] Aisha: Regarding data residency, our legal team requires EU data at rest for EU customers and logs retained for 7 years for audit. How does Redwood handle region pinning and log retention?
[02:04] Daniel: We support region routing policies — requests can be routed to EU-hosted instances. For Hosted we have region-specific deployments; for Dedicated and Private you can run in your chosen region. Audit logs: we capture request/response metadata, admin actions, and we can offer configurable retention policies. Default retention is 90 days for logs in the hosted product, but we can extend or provide export for long-term archival.
[02:26] Priya: Can we get immutable/compliance-grade logs or a mechanism to ship logs to our SIEM?
[02:31] Sofia: Yes, we provide log forwarding to customer destinations (S3 buckets, customer SIEM endpoints) and support write-once storage patterns. We also have tamper-evident audit trails via signed log bundles for Dedicated/Private deployments.
[02:44] Speaker 2 (Redwood): small note, sometimes transcript munges the product names — Redwood Dedicate, sorry, Dedicated.
[02:50] Marcus: About RBAC and SSO, we need SCIM and SAML for provisioning and SSO, plus fine-grained roles so devs can't access production keys. What's your RBAC model?
[03:02] Sofia: We support SSO via SAML 2.0 / OIDC and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is role-based with built-in roles and custom role support for Dedicated/Private — you can restrict access to key management, model deployment, and audit export. In the hosted product we provide separation of roles and ability to restrict token scopes.
[03:21] Tom: Are tokens full-privilege? We need least-privilege tokens for runtime inference calls and stricter access for model uploads.
[03:27] Sofia: Exactly. We recommend issuing scoped API keys for runtime that only allow inference calls, and separate admin keys for model management. Tokens support expiration and rotation policies.
[03:36] Aisha: On SOC 2 coverage — does the Type II report include the entire surface or is it scoped to the hosted control plane? We need to confirm what systems were in scope and the period.
[03:45] Daniel: The SOC 2 Type II is scoped to our hosted inference platform and related control systems; the report includes the period of testing (we'll include dates in the report). For Dedicated and Private we provide a controls addendum showing how responsibilities are shared.
[03:58] Priya: Can you elaborate on shared responsibility for Private deployment? For instance, who is responsible for patching, key storage, and audit logs?
[04:07] Sofia: For Private deployments if Redwood manages the control plane we handle patching of Redwood components we ship; if on-prem, patching of underlying infra often sits with the customer. Key storage is customer-managed if you choose BYOK. Audit logs: we can collect and ship, but retention and long-term archival are customer responsibilities unless contracted otherwise. We'll document this in the controls mapping.
[04:27] Marcus: For our security review we'll need control IDs mapped to our internal control set and proof artifacts — e.g., configuration screenshots, policy docs, runbooks. Do you provide evidence packages?
[04:36] Sofia: Yes, we provide evidence bundles for SOC 2 controls — redactable screenshots, policy excerpts, and attestation letters. We can't share customer data but we can show systemic evidence.
[04:45] Tom: On incident response and breach notifications, what's your SLA? Our procurement wants 24/7 notification within X hours.
[04:53] Daniel: Our standard contractual breach notification is 72 hours; for enterprise we can negotiate shorter windows as part of the contract and include escalation contacts. We also provide post-incident reports and timelines.
[05:05] Aisha: For auditors we may need direct access to logs or a signed letter. Can we grant our auditor Trust Center access or do you prefer pushing bundles?
[05:14] Daniel: We typically grant time-limited Trust Center auditor access and/or provide a secure reviewer link. We'll coordinate with your audit team on format.
[05:22] Priya: One more — how do you handle redaction in reports? We need PII removal but still provide sufficient context for auditors.
[05:28] Sofia: Our redactable reports have PII removed and include annotations on where live data would be. We can produce a version for internal auditors and a more sanitized version for external review.
[05:36] Marcus: Regarding runtime telemetry, do you store full request/response payloads? For HIPAA workloads we need to ensure PHI is not stored.
[05:45] Sofia: We do capture traces and metadata by default; we do not store full prompt/response payloads unless explicitly enabled for debugging or caching. For sensitive workloads we recommend disabling payload logging and enabling prefix/KV cache safeguards. For Dedicated/Private, you can choose not to persist payloads.
[06:03] Tom: Is there a feature to redact specific fields automatically?
[06:07] Sofia: We have configurable scrubbing and token filters and can integrate with webhook-based scrubbers for pre-ingest filtering. We'll include docs.
[06:15] Aisha: About penetration testing — do you publish results or allow customer-commissioned pentests?
[06:21] Daniel: We do annual third-party pentests and provide executive summaries; for Dedicated/Private we often support customer-contracted pentests under a scoping and nondisclosure agreement.
[06:31] Priya: Okay, next practical step — controls mapping and report access. If you can get us the SOC 2 bundle and the mapping sheet, we'll ingest and identify gaps.
[06:41] Daniel: Will do. Sofia, any technical follow-ups to include for the mapping?
[06:44] Sofia: I'll add sections on KMS integration patterns, RBAC examples, log forwarding endpoints, and evidence types for each control. Also note limitations — e.g., default hosted log retention and how to extend.
[06:56] Marcus: For log export, can we SFTP or only cloud storage?
[07:00] Sofia: We support S3, GCS, Azure Blob, and Syslog/SIEM endpoints; SFTP is possible via dedicated export jobs for enterprise customers.
[07:09] Tom: Any compliance certifications for underlying cloud providers? We need to show their SOCs as part of our vendor chain evidence.
[07:16] Sofia: We rely on public cloud providers' authoritative SOC/ISO attestations; in the Trust Center we'll link to the underlying provider assurance statements and note shared controls.
[07:25] Aisha: Great. Recap what we'll receive: redactable SOC 2 Type II, ISO certificate, trust center auditor access, controls mapping spreadsheet, KMS and RBAC docs, and log export instructions.
[07:36] Daniel: Correct. We'll aim to send the SOC 2 bundle and trust center link by 2026-04-01 and the mapping sheet by 2026-04-03.
[07:44] Priya: We'll schedule the follow-up for week of 2026-04-06. Also, we'll confirm residency list by 2026-04-02.
[07:52] Daniel: Sounds good — any last-minute questions?
[07:55] Tom: No, thanks, this was helpful.
[07:58] Speaker 1 (Daniel): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments and links.
[08:03] Aisha: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
